why: Combination Sum: backtracking with a start index. Passing the current index (not i + 1) to the recursive call lets a value be reused, and never going back to earlier indices makes every combination nondecreasing, so no duplicate orderings appear.
hints: [2,2,3] and [2,3,2] and [3,2,2] are the same combination. What rule on the order you pick values makes each combination appear exactly once?
Only pick candidates at index >= the index of the last pick. Recurse with the same index to allow reuse, and stop when the remaining target hits 0 or goes negative.

Sort candidates; dfs(start, remain, path): if remain == 0 record a copy; for i from start, break if candidates[i] > remain, else push, dfs(i, remain - candidates[i]), pop. Sorted order gives lexicographic output.
pitfalls: Recursing with i + 1 forbids reuse and misses [2,2,3].
Starting each level from 0 produces permutations of the same combination.
